title: Bug/#4497 Unable to Cherry Pick Merge Commit Solved
body:
## :bookmark_tabs: Summary

Cherry-pick a merge commit, requires a special flag because merge commits have more than one parent. When you cherry-pick a regular commit, Git knows to take the changes from the parent commit to the chosen commit. In the case of a merge commit, there are multiple parent commits, so you have to specify which parent's context you want to use for the cherry-pick.
If you try to cherry-pick a merge commit without specifying a parent, Git won't know what changes to apply and will prompt you to specify a mainline parent.


Resolves #4497 

## :straight_ruler: Design Decisions

The Pull Request addresses this issue by introducing additional syntax to the parser and modifying the cherryPick function to handle merge commit cherry-picking scenarios properly. Specifically:

A new identifier, PARENT_COMMIT, was introduced in the parser syntax to allow users to specify the parent commit when cherry-picking a merge commit.

The cherryPick function was enhanced to validate and handle the parentCommitId parameter when dealing with merge commits. It now checks if the specified parent commit is an immediate parent of the merge commit being cherry-picked and throws descriptive errors when incorrect usage is detected.
The function also handles tagging and branch checks to ensure the cherry-pick operation's correctness and to provide informative feedback to the user regarding any incorrect usage.

With these enhancements, users can now accurately represent cherry-picking merge commits within their Mermaid Git diagrams, improving the library's functionality and usability for illustrating complex Git workflows. The new syntax and function logic cover various cherry-picking scenarios, providing a robust solution to the initially reported problem.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
One potential change (although we could do this in another PR, since I know this PR has been open for a while). Should we move this check outside of the `if (sourceCommit.type === commitType.MERGE) {` condition?

```suggestion
  }
  if (parentCommitId && !(Array.isArray(sourceCommit.parents) && sourceCommit.parents.includes(parentCommitId))) {
    let error = new Error(
      'Invalid operation: The specified parent commit is not an immediate parent of the cherry-picked commit.'
    );
    throw error;
```

Currently, if we use a bad `parent: "xxx"` field for a cherry-pick that **doesn't target a MERGE**, there's no error, e.g. the following diagram renders correctly without any errors:

````markdown
```mermaid
gitGraph
    commit id: "ZERO"
    branch feature
    branch release
    checkout feature
    commit id: "A"
    commit id: "Not a merge commit"
    checkout main
    merge feature id: "M"
    checkout release
    cherry-pick id: "Not a merge commit" parent: "this-parent-does-not-exist"
```
````
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer identifies a missing edge case: the parent commit validation check is only inside a MERGE condition, so an invalid parent on a non-merge cherry-pick silently succeeds without throwing an error.

comments.author: aloisklink
comments.body:
> because we will not be having `parentCommitId`, for a commit which is not a merge commit

That's the problem, currently in your PR this is allowed. Try testing with [the below diagram](https://deploy-preview-4944--mermaid-js.netlify.app/edit#pako:eNpVTs0KwjAMfpWSs32BnhWPgt6kl6zN1rL1hy4Fx9i7uzIRzSn5frOCSZZAweD5WjA7HcU-JoXg-di7gtE40f0ywlslNDwv95uGD-HIjKmyCOjjFyplkdmb8c8gMhaK3AB2fpbHKW2iWcbEkl5-Zg1wgkBlj7P7f2uLbHoKpKFZLfVYJ2792y7FyumxRAOKS6UT1GyR6exxKBhA9TjNtL0BOtpPMQ):

````markdown
```mermaid
gitGraph
    commit
    branch b
    commit id: "ZERO"
    checkout main
    %% This works, but maybe it should instead throw an error?
    cherry-pick id: "ZERO" parent: "this-parent-does-not-exist"
```
````

If we move this out of the `if (sourceCommit.type === commitType.MERGE)` block, we'd at get an error like `Invalid operation: The specified parent commit is not an immediate parent of the cherry-picked commit.`.

`git cherry-pick COMMIT` with the `--mainline <parent-number>` does the same thing: https://git-scm.com/docs/git-cherry-pick#Documentation/git-cherry-pick.txt---mainlineltparent-numbergt. If you try to use `--mainline <parent-number>` when cherry-picking a non-merge commit, it still works, assuming that the parent does exist on that commit.

comments.author: nirname
comments.body:
I know this is working and we are heading towards another parser, but if there is one more option to this then we probably have to create grammar rules for all the permutations.

If arguments order is the only difference between those repetitive lines I would split them into several grammar rules like this (just an example):

```
cherryPickStatement: CHERRY_PICK commit (cherry_pick_argument)
commit
: COMMIT_TAG [STR | EMPTY_STR]
| COMMIT_ID STR

cherry_pick_argument
: PARENT_COMMIT STR { $$={parentCommit: $STR} }
| COMMIT_TAG [STR | EMPTY_STR]
| COMMIT_ID STR
|
```
etc. Assigning result to $$ will form ascending tree. This way we could avoid bothering about arguments order. But since the whole previous grammar is excessive and redundant I think this is OK.
comments.label_reasoning: The reviewer points out that the grammar rules are repetitive and redundant due to handling all argument order permutations explicitly, and suggests refactoring into composable grammar rules to reduce redundancy.
